decisive_items: acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to their left arm
broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5
Subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery
response.rationale: ACS best encompasses the acute presentation, dynamic ECG changes, and subtotal LAD occlusion despite normal troponin; UA is a narrower subset but lacks the explicit ECG abnormality emphasis, while MI is contradicted by normal troponin.

rejected.why: Normal troponin (<0.05 ng/mL) contradicts myocardial infarction despite suggestive symptoms and angiography.
Unstable angina is plausible but less specific than ACS given the documented ECG T-wave changes and subtotal occlusion; ACS is the broader, more accurate syndrome.
